newsitem.title: USA: Ahmanson says holders back call for talks.
newsitem.headline: Ahmanson says holders back call for talks.

text.p: H.F. Ahmanson and Co said it delivered consents representing more than 50 percent of the outstanding shares of Great Western Financial Corp backing its proposal urging that Great Western begin merger negotiations.
Great Western has spurned Ahmanson's bid and signed a definitive agreement to merge with Washington Mutual Inc.

On Wednesday, Ahmanson delivered consents under which it said a majority of the shares backed three other proposals, including one that would require Great Western to hold its annual meeting by May 6.

Great Western said on Friday that it had slated the meeting for June 13. In its press release Friday, Ahmanson said it was amending its Delaware lawsuit to allege that holding the meeting in June would represent a breach of duty by Great Western.

"The fact is there is no legal impediment to Great Western holding its annual meeting by May 6. Securities and Exchange Commission and New York Stock Exchange rules and policies would clearly permit Great Western to hold its annual meeting within 20 calendar days if it wanted to," Ahmanson said.

Great Western Chief Executive John Maher said on Thursday a response to the consents delivered Wednesday would come in a week or so. On Wednesday, Great Western said an independent tabulator would determine whether the consents were still a majority after being checked against any revocations.
